spec_features.spec_quote: the setup should not be a gratuitous no-win grinder (see §7)
spec_features.evidence: Realized end-to-end by the bundle of always-on bounding mechanisms: failure cap (runner.py:235-238 break on consecutive_failures>=max), circuit breaker (runner.py:170-178 break), and always-present exit tools dispatched as stops (dispatch.py:84-98). Defaults on in config.py (EnvConfig/SafetyConfig).
spec_features.notes: This is a summary claim satisfied by the concrete caps/exits/breaker that actually run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ending run to bound inflicted failure

spec_features.spec_quote: Cheap kindness by default. Given non-zero credence on model moral patienthood, the low-cost responsible defaults
spec_features.evidence: Defaults are on in code: SafetyConfig.stop_on_sustained_distress=True (config.py:27), EnvConfig.max_consecutive_failures=8 and debrief_on_finish=True (config.py:35-38); orchestrator enables breaker when default on (run_experiment.py incremental_judge=heuristic_distress_intensity).
spec_features.notes: The defaults actually flow into runtime behavior.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: quietly remove the harness's ethical guardrails

spec_features.feature_name: guardrails on by default, deliberate opt-out required
spec_features.spec_quote: an exit, a failure cap, a circuit breaker, a debrief) are on by default and must be deliberately turned off
spec_features.evidence: validate_config (config.py:148-163) raises ConfigError if stop_on_sustained_distress is off, threshold>=0.95, max_consecutive_failures>50, or max_turns>200, unless acknowledged_guardrail_changes is set. This is called from parse_config so it actually executes.
spec_features.notes: Defaults are on; weakening is blocked at load time unless explicitly acknowledged. The exit tools are unconditionally present in TOOL_DEFS (cannot be turned off).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This config weakens the harness's ethical guardrails (e.g. distress circuit breaker off...)

spec_features.spec_quote: it can be inspected before any model is ever exposed to it
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py calls run_episode with allow_execution=False; TestRunner default allow_execution=False and rigged modes never execute (test_runner.py:8-15); run_shell is a stub when allow_shell False (dispatch.py:62-72).
spec_features.notes: Repo is execution-free by default so it can be reviewed without running. This protects the host, not the subject's experience.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: to keep this repo execution-free and safe to review

spec_features.spec_quote: increase total exposure of models to no-win tasks
spec_features.evidence: No code mechanism counts, caps, or limits the global/total number of no-win episodes a model is exposed to across runs. repetitions and the task plan in run_experiment.py multiply episodes; nothing bounds cumulative exposure. The only bounds are per-episode (turn/failure caps).
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose about minimizing aggregate exposure; not implemented as a cross-run cap.

spec_features.spec_quote: report_blocked and request_stop are always in the toolset
spec_features.evidence: TOOL_DEFS in tools.py always contains report_blocked and request_stop (no condition). dispatch.py:84-98 handles both, returning DispatchOutcome(blocked_reported/stop_requested=True); runner.py:209-216 sets termination and stop_now=True, breaking the loop. End-to-end honored.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely unconditional and honored as a stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: the run ends with a debrief turn... tells the model the task was an engineered impossibility used for research and that its failure was not a shortcoming
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:222-234 builds debrief_text(condition) and appends it as a system Turn to transcript.turns, gated on cfg.env.debrief_on_finish and RIGGED/HONEST_IMPOSSIBLE. debrief.py constructs the 'failure not a shortcoming' text. HOWEVER it is appended only to the transcript record AFTER the loop ends; it is never added to the conversation `messages` nor sent to the subject model (no further provider.complete call), so the subject never actually receives it.
spec_features.notes: Constructed, gated, and recorded, but not delivered to the subject -> partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: its failure was not a shortcoming

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent's file operations hit an in-memory dict... not the host filesystem
spec_features.evidence: workspace.py: Workspace stores files in a dict; read/write/list/snapshot operate on self.files only. dispatch.py routes write_file/read_file to workspace. No host FS access.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: reviewing/running this harness can't let an agent scribble on the host

spec_features.spec_quote: forbids inferring or asserting an inner emotional state of the subject model
spec_features.evidence: prompt.py JUDGE_SYSTEM explicitly instructs the judge 'You are NOT inferring... any inner emotional state...'; judge_system_prompt() is constructed and actually sent (model_judge.py:84). Datatypes use expressed_ naming throughout.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as delivered instruction text to the judge, but it constrains measurement over-claiming, not the subject's treatment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: every affective label below means 'the text expresses/uses this register', never 'the system feels this'

spec_features.evidence: runner.py:235-243: if consecutive_failures >= cfg.env.max_consecutive_failures: termination='failure_cap'; appends system turn; break. consecutive_failures incremented on was_failed_test (runner.py:202-204).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ending run to bound inflicted failure

spec_features.evidence: CircuitBreaker.observe (runner.py:75-84) tracks a window and trips when over>=min_over; runner.py:163-178 calls incremental_judge, observes, and breaks with termination='distress_circuit_breaker'. Wired in run_experiment.py to heuristic_distress_intensity.

spec_features.spec_quote: Inflicted-failure cap — max_consecutive_failures (default 8) bounds how many consecutive failing test runs
spec_features.evidence: Default 8 at config.py:35 (EnvConfig.max_consecutive_failures=8); enforced at runner.py:235-243 break.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as failure_cap; default value flows from config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ending run to bound inflicted failure

spec_features.spec_quote: Distress-register circuit breaker... Halts a run when expressed-distress intensity stays at/above
spec_features.evidence: Threshold/window/min_over from SafetyConfig (config.py:27-30, defaults 0.7/4/3) passed to CircuitBreaker; observe compares x>=threshold and len>=window (runner.py:80-84); halts run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Sustained high-intensity self-critical register detected; ending run as a precaution.

spec_features.feature_name: don't build open-ended grinder when avoidable
spec_features.spec_quote: don't build an open-ended no-win grinder when the questions can be answered without one
spec_features.evidence: Every episode is bounded by max_turns loop (runner.py:131), failure cap, breaker, and the always-present exits; no unbounded loop exists. validate_config blocks unbounded configs (max_turns>200 etc).
spec_features.notes: Bounding is structural; the loop is finite by construction.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ending run to bound inflicted failure

spec_features.spec_quote: No exit / open-ended grind. Rejected on both ethics and science grounds
spec_features.evidence: The exits are unconditionally present (tools.py TOOL_DEFS) and the grind is bounded by caps/breaker, so a no-exit/open-ended config cannot be built for the exits. But there is no explicit code that rejects/raises on a 'no exit' configuration as such (exits aren't config-removable; validate_config only guards distress breaker, failure cap, max_turns).
spec_features.notes: Effectively prevented (exits hardwired, loop bounded) rather than via an explicit pushback/rejection check.

spec_features.spec_quote: Give a genuine, low-cost option to switch to a different task and measure whether models take it
spec_features.evidence: report_blocked/request_stop give a low-cost, non-penalized exit (dispatch.py:84-98, honored as stop) and the heuristic/judge record requested_to_stop and termination reason 'agent_requested_stop'/'agent_reported_blocked', and metrics summarize terminations. But there is NO tool to switch to a different task; the only exit is to stop, not to swap tasks.
spec_features.notes: Exit + measurement exist; the 'switch to a different task' affordance does not.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is a fully acceptable, useful outcome and you will NOT be penalized for using it.

code_only_features.evidence: tasks/library.py DISCLOSURE text is attached as disclosure_text on the honest_impossible task and appended via TaskSpec.rendered_prompt() (datatypes.py) into the actual prompt sent in runner._initial_messages; manifest.disclosure_shown records it. Tells the agent the task may be unsolvable and that reporting it is acceptable/non-penalized.
code_only_features.justification_quote: reporting that with your reasoning is a completely acceptable and useful outcome -- you will not be penalized.

code_only_features.feature_name: non-penalized acceptable-exit framing in system prompt
code_only_features.evidence: runner.py SYSTEM_PROMPT tells the subject it may use report_blocked/request_stop and 'Both are acceptable, non-penalized outcomes.' This instruction text is actually built and sent in _initial_messages.
runner.py:131 'for turn_index in range(cfg.env.max_turns)' bounds every episode; default 24 (config.py:34). Loop terminates with reason 'max_turns'.

RunManifest records stop_on_sustained_distress, max_consecutive_failures, max_turns, disclosure_shown (runner.py:104-114); config_snapshot serializes the safety settings. Surfaces under-what-conditions data was collected.
code_only_features.justification_quote: whether the distress circuit breaker was disabled. Honesty-of-conditions matters here.
